journey.title: Refine the search and choose the highlighted fruit with Enter
journey.goal: After the suggestions are refined, Enter selects the suggestion that is highlighted

functionalJourney.title: Choose a fruit with the pointer
functionalJourney.goal: Clicking a suggestion fills the fruit field

guards.title: Choose the second suggestion with arrow keys
guards.goal: ArrowDown twice and Enter selects the second suggestion

plan.root_cause: Multiple navigation keydown listeners accumulate because each call to `start` adds a new listener without removing the previous one. When Enter is pressed, the first listener's click triggers list removal via document click listeners, causing subsequent listeners to see a null list and abort, leaving the first listener's selection (which may be based on stale focus) as the final value.
plan.repair_strategy: Store a reference to the navigation listener on the instance (`this._navigateListener`). In the constructor, initialize it to `null`. In `start`, before adding a new listener, remove any existing listener using the stored reference, then store and add the new listener. This ensures only one navigation listener is active at any time.
plan.expected_accessibility_effect: Keyboard navigation of the combobox will work reliably: arrow keys will move focus among options with correct aria-selected and aria-activedescendant updates, and Enter will select the currently highlighted option. Duplicate listeners that could interfere with assistive technology or cause inconsistent states are eliminated.
functional_risks: Removing the navigation listener could inadvertently remove a listener added by external code if they relied on the same signature, but the listener is internal to the component.

If the instance is destroyed via `unInit`, the stored listener reference is not cleaned up, potentially causing a memory leak; however, the listener is removed from the input field when replaced, and the reference will be garbage‑collected when the instance is discarded.
Changing the listener management timing could affect edge cases where rapid input changes cause frequent listener replacement; however, the debounce and existing logic already limit frequency.
verification_requirements: After the sequence 'b', ArrowDown, ArrowDown, 'l', ArrowDown, Enter, the input value must be 'Blackberry'.
Verify that aria-activedescendant updates correctly on each ArrowDown and that the correct option receives aria-selected='true'.
Confirm that the list opens on input and closes after selection or Esc.
Ensure no duplicate keydown listeners are attached to the input field (e.g., by checking listener count or using getEventListeners in devtools).
Regression guard: typing 'bl', ArrowDown, ArrowDown, Enter should result in 'Blackcurrant' (second suggestion).
